title: QuantumHarbor POC: Assurance & Evidence Playbook
executive_summary:
Purpose: This playbook collects the security and compliance responses, evidence index, and workshop outcomes for the QuantumHarbor POC. Goal is to give the customer a compact, actionable assurance packet they can use for internal review and audit planning.

High-level outcome: Redwood will provide a dedicated POC deployment in a customer VPC peering arrangement (staging) with customer-managed KMS keys. We validated encryption-in-transit, encryption-at-rest using CMKs, logging to customer SIEM via syslog, and an initial penetration test plan. Remaining items are a short list of evidence exports and an agreement on retention windows for logs and traces.
scope_and_objectives:
Scope: POC environment only (non-production), 2-week engagement, single model endpoint (gpt-large-quantized) behind private subnet.
Objectives: 1) Demonstrate network isolation and access controls; 2) Provide evidence artifacts for standard security questionnaire items; 3) Run a focused red-team exercise on the POC perimeter; 4) Confirm logging/forwarding into QuantumHarbor SIEM and provide retention options.
Out of scope: Full SOC2 audit, production data residency guarantees beyond region agreement, and long-term SLAs (these are covered under Dedicated/Private contracts).
questionnaire_responses:
Q: Where do you store customer data?
A: POC data stored in customer VPC (EBS volumes attached to Redwood-managed instances) and optionally mirrored to customer S3 bucket when requested. Data at rest encrypted with customer-managed KMS key.

Q: Do you use HSM for keys?
A: Support for BYOK with cloud KMS (customer-managed keys) is supported; we can integrate with customer HSM via KMS import or external key manager in the Private deployment. For the hosted POC, we recommend customer KMS in their cloud account.

Q: How are models and weights handled?
A: Model binaries used for the POC are pulled from Redwood's internal model registry and run ephemeral on the POC instances. No model weights are exported to customer storage unless explicitly requested in writing.

Q: What logs do you provide?
A: Access logs, model inference audit events (non-input token content), system metrics, and instance-level system logs. Sensitive prompt inputs can be redacted per agreement.

Q: Incident response contact?
A: Primary IR: Aisha Patel (solutions-eng), Backup IR: Marco Ruiz (security). All incidents follow Redwood IR runbook, shared via the Confluence link in linked_artifacts.
deployment_architecture_summary:
Network: Customer VPC peering (one-way accept), Redwood-managed compute in customer subnets with strict SG rules limiting outbound to SIEM and updates.
Identity: IAM roles for provisioning scoped tightly to resource tags; ephemeral short-lived service credentials for runtime processes.
Encryption: EBS/S3 encrypted with customer CMK; TLS1.3 for all in-flight traffic; mTLS between inference runtime and control-plane when applicable.
Key management: Customer-managed KMS CMK used for EBS and object encryption. KMS policy exported as part of evidence bundle.
Observability: Logs forwarded to customer SIEM via syslog endpoint; metrics to a read-only metrics dashboard with token-based access; trace sampling at 0.5% for POC by default (configurable).

workshop_notes:
Attendees: QuantumHarbor security, infra leads; Redwood solutions and security.

Key discussion bullets:
- QuantumHarbor requires BYOK and 7-year access/archival logs for certain regulated flows; we proposed tiered retention to reduce cost.
- Customer asked for guarantee that model inputs would not be retained longer than 24 hours — Redwood offered redaction policy and configurable retention TTL for POC artifacts.
- Demonstrated VPC peering setup and showed sample syslog ingestion into customer's Splunk instance.
- Agreed to run a focused perimeter pentest after evidence package is delivered; scope limited to edge and admin console access.

Open/parking-lot items:
- Confirm whether customer wants model weights exported for offline validation (action item below).
- Decide on default trace sampling rates for PII-sensitive routes.
- Legal to review retention SLA addendum (QuantumHarbor legal team).
risk_gaps_and_mitigations:
Identified risk: Admin console accounts used for initial provisioning have broader privileges than ideal. Mitigation: rotate to least-privilege automation roles prior to handoff; provide audit trail of the rotation.

Identified risk: Retention of raw prompts in debug logs. Mitigation: apply redaction hook to runtime logs for endpoints marked PII; provide proof-of-redaction via sample outputs.

Identified risk: Customer requires on-prem HSM integration for keys. Mitigation: roadmap note — Private deployment supports HSM; for this POC, offer a short-term compensating control (KMS in customer account + strict access logs).

notes_to_self:
- Keep evidence filenames stable (use numeric prefixes) to make it easy for automation to pull.
- Ask Legal for a short retention addendum template for POCs that can be attached to the SOW.
- If customer insists on on-prem HSM, route to Private deployment lead and flag for timeline impact.
